The *Saṅkiccattheragāthā* (Thag 11.1) is a verse text belonging to the *Theragāthā* collection in the Pali Sutta Piṭaka, comprising the verses attributed to the elder Saṅkicca [SuttaCentral]. In modern scholarship and translation, the text has been rendered into multiple languages, including an English translation by Bhikkhu Sujato [SuttaCentral]. It is also explicitly cited or mentioned in later non-canonical Pali literature, specifically in the *Milindapañha* (Mil 3.2.4, *Paṭisandahanapuggalavediyanapañha*) [SuttaCentral].

Curated passage-level parallels identified by SuttaCentral link the text to other poetic collections within the Pali canon, notably the *Khadiravaniyarevatattheragāthā* (Thag 14.1), the *Sāriputtattheragāthā* (Thag 17.2), and the *Sukhavihārijātaka* (Ja 10), alongside thematic similarities with the *Nisabhattheragāthā* (Thag 2.38) [SuttaCentral]. 

Automated text-reuse analyses by DharmaNexus confirm extensive internal Pali parallels, registering 55 matches across 9 texts [DharmaNexus]. In particular, segments 8.1–9.4 represent a formulaic or shared stock of verses that recur verbatim or near-verbatim in Thag 14.1 (where DharmaNexus agrees with SuttaCentral's curated parallel), the *Mahāmoggallānattheragāthā* (Thag 20.1), the *Raṭṭhapālattheragāthā* (Thag 16.4), and several *Therī-apadāna* texts (Thi-Ap 17, 20, and 24) [DharmaNexus]. The full sequence of verses (§§1.1–11.5) is preserved and commented upon in the *Theragāthā-aṭṭhakathā*, with additional substantial reuse found in the *Therīgāthā-aṭṭhakathā* [DharmaNexus]. Cross-tradition alignments computed by DharmaNexus also note a textual match between segments 9.1–9.3 and the Chinese translation of the *Madhyama-āgama* (T 26) [DharmaNexus].
